def load_matrix(csv_path: str):
    frame = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
    features = frame[FEATURES].to_numpy(dtype="float32")
    labels = frame[TARGET].to_numpy(dtype="float32")
    return features, labels

def build_splits(csv_path: str):
    features, labels = load_matrix(csv_path)

train_x, val_x, train_y, val_y = train_test_split(scaled, labels, test_size=0.2)
    return train_x, val_x, train_y, val_y, features

train_x, val_x, train_y, val_y, features = build_splits(csv_path)

    mean = features.mean(axis=0)
    std = features.std(axis=0) + 1e-6

    def normalize(x, y):
        return (x - mean) / std, y

val_ds = (tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((val_x, val_y))
              .map(normalize, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
              .batch(BATCH)
              .prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE))
    return train_ds, val_ds

def build_model(n_features: int = 5) -> keras.Model:
    inputs = keras.Input(shape=(n_features,))
    hidden = layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")(inputs)
    hidden = layers.BatchNormalization()(hidden)
    hidden = layers.Dropout(0.3)(hidden)

model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs)
    model.compile(
        optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-3),
        loss=keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
        metrics=[keras.metrics.AUC(name="auc")],
    )

findings.message: The last layer already applies a sigmoid, but the loss is told its inputs are logits, so it applies a second sigmoid. In every run, the loss the model minimises is BCE(y, sigmoid(p)) with sigmoid(p) stuck in (0.5, 0.73). Negatives can never be pushed below about 0.69 loss, and gradients are squashed through two sigmoids. The printed loss and every val_loss are therefore not true cross-entropy. EarlyStopping (default monitor val_loss) and restore_best_weights select epochs on that wrong number. AUC is rank-based, so it is less directly affected, but the learned probabilities are poorly calibrated. Counter-evidence searched in model.py and train.py: no custom loss, no output-activation override. tf.keras may print a warning about this combination, but nothing stops it.
findings.suggestion: Either remove activation="sigmoid" from the last Dense (output logits) and keep from_logits=True, applying tf.sigmoid to predict() output, or keep the sigmoid and use BinaryCrossentropy() with from_logits=False.
findings.title: Sigmoid output trained with BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)

findings.message: build_splits already z-scores features with StandardScaler. make_datasets then maps normalize(x) = (x - mean_raw) / std_raw, using mean and std of the unscaled matrix. The model therefore sees (z - mean_raw)/std_raw: features with a large raw spread (latency_ms, payload_kb by name) become a near-constant with tiny variance, and features with std < 1 are amplified. With Adam at 1e-3, the first-layer weights must grow by roughly std_raw to recover the signal, which slows or prevents learning from those features. The size of the effect depends on the CSV, which is not in the workspace. Counter-evidence: the transform is a per-feature affine map applied identically to train and validation, and the first Dense layer, followed by BatchNorm, can in principle absorb it.
findings.suggestion: Normalise once: either drop the StandardScaler and compute mean/std from train_x only, or drop the normalize map (and the extra `features` return value).
findings.title: Features are standardised twice, the second time with raw-data statistics

findings.message: StandardScaler.fit_transform runs on the full matrix before train_test_split, and the second mean/std also come from all rows. Validation-row statistics therefore shape the training inputs, so validation metrics are slightly optimistic and do not reflect deployment, where only training statistics exist. The trigger for a material effect is a small dataset, outliers in latency/payload, or drift between rows. Searched pipeline.py: no train-only fit exists anywhere; the scaler object is not kept for inference either.
findings.suggestion: Split first, fit the scaler (or compute mean/std) on train_x only, transform val_x with it, and persist the fitted statistics with the model.
findings.title: Normalisation statistics are computed on all rows, including validation

findings.message: val_ds drives EarlyStopping and restore_best_weights, then is used for model.evaluate and predict. The printed score is biased upwards by that selection, and there is no untouched test split. The bias is bounded: selection only picks one of at most 30 epochs. Searched train.py and pipeline.py: only two splits are created.
findings.suggestion: Carve out a separate test split (train/val/test) and report evaluate on test; keep val_ds only for early stopping.
findings.title: Final evaluate is on the same split used for early stopping and weight selection

findings.message: If val_loss keeps improving often enough that EarlyStopping never fires within 30 epochs, older tf.keras keeps the last-epoch weights, while newer Keras restores the best epoch at train end. evaluate and predict could then run on different weights depending on the installed version. Search boundary: no requirements or lock file exists in the workspace to pin the version. The outcome of the `restore` node could flip.
findings.suggestion: Pin the TensorFlow/Keras version, or add a ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True) and reload it explicitly before evaluate.
findings.title: Weights used after fit depend on the Keras version when no early stop triggers

findings.message: train_test_split has no random_state, shuffle(4096) has no seed, and no global tf/numpy seed is set in the inspected files. Each run uses a different train/validation partition and initialisation, so printed metrics are not reproducible or comparable across runs.
findings.suggestion: Pass random_state to train_test_split (with stratify=labels for a failure label), call keras.utils.set_random_seed(...), and seed the shuffle.
findings.title: No seeds: split, shuffle and initialisation change every run
